summary: Saburō Hasegawa studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1926 to 1929. He held posts as a teacher at the American Academy of Asian Studies (~1954–1955) and at the California College of the Arts (~1955–1957).
Sachindra Kumar Maity was an Indologist and historian who studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham (~1954–1956). He held an academic post at Jadavpur University from around 1957 to 1986.

Sadajiro Sugiura, a scholar of philosophy and Indology, studied at Rikkyo University, the University of Pennsylvania, and Philadelphia Divinity School. He held posts at Pennsylvania, the Army War College (1903), and Rikkyo University (1907, 1931–1932).

Said Reza Huseini works in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed his studies at King's College London, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and Leiden University (~2016–2021).

Saiyid Athar Abbas Rizvi, a scholar of history, Indology, and religious studies, studied under Mohammad Habib and at Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University. He held positions at Jammu and Kashmir, SOAS, JNU, and the Australian National University (1967–1986).

Sakunoshin Motoda, a scholar of religious studies, studied at Kenyon College (~1888–1891), the University of Pennsylvania (~1891–1895), and Columbia University (~1895–1896). He held a post at Rikkyo University from around 1907 to 1928.
Sakutaro Fujioka was a Japanese studies and history scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1894 to 1897 and later held a post there from around 1900 to 1910.

Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under teachers including Ngawang Kunga Rinchen, Tenzin Gyatso, and Chogye Trichen, and served as abbot at Sakya Monastery until 2017.

Sakyong Mipham, active in religious and Buddhist studies, studied at Oxford, Namdroling Monastery, and under teachers including Chögyam Trungpa and Dilgo Khyentse. He served as a board member at Naropa University until 2018.

Sallie B. King is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religion. She studied under Leon Hurvitz at the University of British Columbia (~1973–1975) and served as Professor of Philosophy and Religion at James Madison University (~1990–2008).

Sally J. Sutherland Goldman works in Indology and linguistics. She studied at UC Berkeley (PhD 1979) and under Shivram Dattatray Joshi and Shrinivasa Shastri, later holding an academic post at UC Berkeley (attested 1996).
Sally McAra specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed an MA at the University of Auckland (1999–2000), where she studied under Christine Dureau and Karen Nero.
Sally Mellick Cutler, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, earned her D.Phil. at the University of Oxford by 1993. She served as manager of the Pali Text Society Office (attested 1997).

Salomon Lefmann was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Franz Bopp at Humboldt University and at Münster, Heidelberg, and Paris. He held academic posts at Heidelberg University starting in 1866, becoming associate professor in 1870.
Sam van Schaik is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from the University of Manchester (~1997–2000). He has held positions at SOAS and at the British Library since 1999.
Samani Pratibha Pragya works in Indology and religious studies. She earned her PhD from SOAS University of London and served as a research assistant there (attested 2020).

Samdhong Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy scholar. Educated at Drepung and Gyuto monasteries under teachers including Tenzin Gyatso, he served as Director of the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies from 1971 to 2001.

Samten Gyaltsen Karmay is a Tibetologist who studied at Drepung Monastery and SOAS under David Snellgrove. He held positions at SOAS, Collège de France, Paris Nanterre, and CNRS (from 1980), and served as IATS President (1995–2000).

Samuel Beal, a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies, studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (BA ~1843–1847). He served at Bramham College, the India Office Library, and held a professorship in Chinese at University College London from 1877.

Samuel George Frederick Brandon was a scholar of religious studies and history who studied at the University of Leeds (~1930–1934) and held an academic post at the University of Manchester from around 1951 to 1971.
